body.statement: For every finite family of real polynomials, a finite sign-invariant cylindrical algebraic decomposition adapted to that family can be computed. Its cylindrical lifting decides every Boolean combination of their sign conditions, yields an equivalent quantifier-free formula after projection, and represents sections by continuous semialgebraic real-root functions. For rational input, real-algebraic sample points and boundary roots admit square-free polynomials, rational isolating intervals, and Thom derivative-sign encodings.

source.locator: Section~2.2, Definition~2.3 and the theorem labeled \(5{:}\mathrm{thm{:}cad}\), the immediately following quantifier-elimination paragraph, and Section~2.3 on isolating intervals and Thom encodings
source.verbatim_statement: For every finite set \(\mathcal P\) of polynomials in \(\mathbb R[X_1,\ldots,X_k]\), there is a cylindrical decomposition of \(\mathbb R^k\) adapted to \(\mathcal P\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from the TeX source of arXiv:1409.1534 at the stated theorem; the surrounding definition supplies continuous semialgebraic sections and the following paragraph states quantifier elimination.
